chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from the multitude of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque) is not valid for less than three days. Whoever performs I'tikaf must fast. It is appropriate for the one performing I'tikaf, when he enters it, to make a condition (of intention), just as the one who enters Ihram makes a condition.

key_terms.الاعتكاف: I'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque for worship)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions and minimum duration for I'tikaf according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records in *al-Istibsar* that Imam al-Sadiq (AS) sets the minimum duration for I'tikaf at three days, linking it obligatorily with fasting to emphasize spiritual discipline. The instruction to make a specific condition (*shart*) upon entry mirrors the ritual precision of Ihram, highlighting the transition from worldly affairs to exclusive devotion within the mosque.
